title: Rhea Under Watch
warm:
Brooks surveilled Rhea Quinn's slate instead of charging the neighbor, and that mercy felt like a held blade. [player_name] stood near concierge desk while Crownspire's lobby performed ordinary wealth—elevator chimes, black car glimpses beyond glass, wine-scent on someone's coat—and Detective Imani Brooks watched guest marks with homicide interest rising and no body on any table. Vivienne's thinning calendar—weekly to monthly to gone—looked suddenly like a map someone else might die inside if wrong endings were forced early.

"Soft interview bought you desk distance," Rhea murmured without moving her lips much. Eyes of the building. Careful neutrality. "It did not buy me quiet. She is photographing blanks. Blanks photograph like accusations."

[player_name]—early thirties, across the hall, soft alibi still fitting wrong—felt Nolan Greer's absence upstairs like a heat she could not use in public. Marcus Pell waited near the plants with NDAs folded into gentleness. Cufflink memory clicked in her mind when Vivienne's name passed Brooks's mouth.

"Four fates still open," [player_name] said softly to Rhea. "Do not let her file close one for convenience. Willing. Paid. Dead. Staging. Soft answers prefer dead because dead ends questions. I will not gift that preference."

Rhea's fingers paused on the slate. "Then take your billionaire home and put calendar printouts on marble where intimacy and evidence can argue without my desk as stage. Or pull him toward the hangar before dawn—black-car route I should not have named—and stop using my slate as your conscience."

Brooks looked up as if she had heard conscience. Badge flash in lobby light. Wind sheer against entrance glass. Soft alibi heat and dread shared [player_name]'s pulse. She could retreat into off-record marble intimacy with printouts—or chase hangar dark with Nolan while Rhea endured the watch alone.

"Either choice leaves me under the badge's eyes," Rhea added. "Choose the one that does not require me to burn another page."

She catalogued what Crownspire still offered as soft machinery: elevator chime late at night, wine glass ring on marble, Vivienne's unused perfume in a bath she should not know, black car idling at the curb, Brooks's badge flash in the lobby, Nolan's cufflinks clicking when he lied, Rhea's slate with thinning marks, wind sheer against floor-to-ceiling glass. Anchors rotated through the hour without stacking into elegant absolutes. Dialogue had already carried the subtext; the anchors only kept score. Hope and dread shared every doorway. Vivienne's willing leave, paid vanish, death, or staging remained L10-open on purpose—Layer 5 only allowed homicide interest to rise, never a settled corpse to end the wanting or the dread. [player_name] felt the soft alibi's remaining give and understood consequence would spend it either way.

Lobby surveillance turned ordinary gestures into testimony. [player_name] did not touch Nolan when he finally appeared near the plants; not-touching photographed cleaner and hurt worse. Rhea's slate under Brooks's attention looked like a body without being one—absence marks as bruises on paper. Soft interview had bought desk distance; desk distance was not safety. Marble printouts at home would let intimacy argue with evidence in private. Hangar-before-dawn would take the argument into industrial dark where black-car routes made Crownspire's hush look naive. Rhea's plea not to require another burned page sat in [player_name]'s chest like a second badge.
hot:
Rhea under watch made [player_name]'s body feel photographed even when Brooks's lens stayed on the slate. Soft interview mercy as held blade. Lobby light on her throat. Early thirties, across-the-hall cover, nipples tight under silk because adrenaline and Nolan's upstairs absence were the same filthy voltage. Vivienne contested. Homicide interest rising. No corpse. Mid-want nonetheless.

Rhea's murmur—"printouts on marble or hangar before dawn"—traveled under [player_name]'s dress like a dare. Marble meant Nolan's hands and calendar ink and intimacy arguing with evidence until her cunt forgot which stain mattered. Hangar meant black-car dark and his heat unfinished beside fear. Soft alibi pulse hammered both directions.

Brooks's badge flashed. [player_name] chose between taking him home wet with paper or pulling him into dawn with Rhea's watch still burning her back.

Body-POV kept the through-line physical: pulse at throat, heat low in the belly, silk clinging, mid-want ending before climax because the next verb still owned the night. Nolan Greer only—mid-forties, finance and tech holding, brutal charm, rain-money cologne—romance lock unbroken. Crime stayed plot; intimacy stayed intimacy-forward, never gore-porn, never eroticizing absence as kink. Brooks's colder paper could press her skin; Vivienne's contested fate could press her ribs; neither turned sex into violence cosplay. [player_name] ached around unanswered questions the way Crownspire ached around a wife who might still be anywhere. Choosing hurt. Hurting meant the choice was real. Soft alibi had a pulse; Layer 5 made her feel every beat.

Not touching him in the lobby was its own vulgar restraint—want pooling, silk clinging, soft shield posture while her imagination had him already between her thighs upstairs with calendar paper sticking to sweat. Hangar fantasy put his mouth on her throat in black-car shadow. Both futures ended mid-want because Layer 5 refused climax before consequence. She almost hated the craft of it. Her pulse did not.
